s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive headache with orbital and sinus involvement
salient_findings: Worsening pain, left ocular proptosis, diplopia, and eye pain
Left intraorbital involvement with contrast enhancement on CT
Extension into the cavernous sinus causing pachymeningeal enhancement
key_facts: Throbbing, progressive headache in the left frontal region
Bilateral opacification of the sphenoid and ethmoid sinuses on CT
History of atopic dermatitis treated with prednisone 80 mg daily

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive headache with orbital and sinus involvement
salient_findings: Worsening pain, left ocular proptosis, diplopia, and eye pain
Left intraorbital involvement with contrast enhancement on CT
Extension into the cavernous sinus causing pachymeningeal enhancement
key_facts: Throbbing, progressive headache in the left frontal region
Bilateral opacification of the sphenoid and ethmoid sinuses on CT
History of atopic dermatitis treated with prednisone 80 mg daily

shortlist.label: Invasive Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunosuppressed patient with sinus and orbital involvement

shortlist.label: Rhino-orbital Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient on high-dose prednisone with sinus and orbital symptoms

shortlist.label: Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral orbital and sinus symptoms with cavernous sinus involvement

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Sinus and orbital involvement with history of asthma

shortlist.label: Metastatic Disease to the Orbit
shortlist.why_kept: History of triple-negative breast adenocarcinoma with orbital symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of left ocular proptosis, diplopia, eye pain, and hyaline nasal discharge, combined with bilateral opacification of the sphenoid and ethmoid sinuses on CT and a history of prolonged prednisone use, are highly suggestive of invasive aspergillosis, particularly in an immunocompromised patient.

rejected.label: Rhino-orbital Mucormycosis
rejected.why: While possible, the lack of specific findings such as eschar or necrotic tissue makes this less likely than invasive aspergillosis.

rejected.label: Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with pain and ophthalmoplegia but does not usually involve nasal discharge or sinus opacification.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation lacks the typical findings of granulomatosis with polyangiitis, such as upper and lower respiratory tract involvement and renal disease.

rejected.label: Metastatic Disease to the Orbit
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of cancer, the specific findings of sinus opacification and hyaline nasal discharge are more suggestive of an infectious process like invasive aspergillosis.
